sections.heading: Overview
sections.wikitext:
The song is about a man who is shocked to discover that his [[high school]] crush appeared in a [[centerfold]] spread for an unspecified men's magazine.<ref name="dean">{{cite book|last=Dean|first=Maury|title=Rock N Roll Gold Rush: A Singles Un-Cyclopedia|publisher=Algora|year=2003|isbn=978-0-87586-207-1|page=330}}</ref> The song's narrator is torn between conflicting feelings: his disappointment due to what he perceives as her loss of innocence, and his lust until the end of the song.<ref name=dean />

The song was the band's biggest hit and the only one to reach the top of the US charts. It was released in the fall of 1981, and eventually went to number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in February 1982, and stayed there for six weeks. It was the first single released from the album ''Freeze Frame'' and the [[music video]] for the song was an early staple on recently launched [[MTV]]. It also peaked at number one in Australia and Canada.

In February 1982, after the song hit No. 1 in the US, "Centerfold" peaked at No. 3 in the [[UK Singles Chart|UK Top 40]], earning the J. Geils Band their only major hit single in the UK, although follow-up "[[Freeze Frame (song)|Freeze-Frame]]" would also peak within the top 40 at No. 27.

''[[Record World]]'' called it a "clever rocker" and said that "the na-na chorus and Peter Wolf's carefree vocals add up to an [[album-oriented rock|AOR]]-pop hit."<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=November 7, 1981|page=1|accessdate=2023-03-02|title=Hits of the Week|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/80s/81/RW-1981-11-07.pdf}}</ref>

In 2018, the song was ranked at No. 66 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s All Time Top Songs.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-60.shtml |title=Billboard Hot 100 Chart 50th Anniversary |magazine=Billboard |access-date=1 August 2018}}</ref>  ''Ultimate Classic Rock'' critic Michael Gallucci rated it to be the band's all-time greatest song.<ref>{{cite web|title=Top 10 J. Geils Band Songs |url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/j-geils-band-songs/|accessdate=2022-06-15|author=Gallucci, Michael|publisher=Ultimate Classic Rock|date=February 20, 2016}}</ref>

The song's narrator is torn between conflicting feelings: his disappointment due to what he perceives as her loss of innocence, and his lust until the end of the song.

The song was the band's biggest hit and the only one to reach the top of the US charts. It was released in the fall of 1981, and eventually went to number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 in February 1982, and stayed there for six weeks. It was the first single released from the album Freeze Frame and the music video for the song was an early staple on recently launched MTV. It also peaked at number one in Australia and Canada.

In February 1982, after the song hit No. 1 in the US, "Centerfold" peaked at No. 3 in the UK Top 40, earning the J. Geils Band their only major hit single in the UK, although follow-up "Freeze-Frame" would also peak within the top 40 at No. 27.

Record World called it a "clever rocker" and said that "the na-na chorus and Peter Wolf's carefree vocals add up to an AOR-pop hit."

In 2018, the song was ranked at No. 66 on Billboard{{'}}s All Time Top Songs.  Ultimate Classic Rock critic Michael Gallucci rated it to be the band's all-time greatest song.
